lessons.title: Chi sono
lessons.outcome: Say who you are with essere and avere: name, city, nationality, age and job.

activities.body: To say who you are, start with io (or leave it out), then a form of essere, then your name, your city or your job. Age is different: it uses avere.
activities.tip: Age takes avere, not essere: ho ventotto anni is literally 'I have twenty-eight years'. Italiano ends in -o for a man and -a for a woman.

activities.en: I am Anna and I am from Rome.
activities.answer: Io sono Anna e sono di Roma.
accepted: Sono Anna e sono di Roma.
activities.explanation: Sono works with or without io. Di + a city says where you are from.
activities.hint: Start with who, then the verb.

activities.template: Ciao, io ____ Marco e ____ ventotto anni.
activities.en: Hi, I am Marco and I am twenty-eight years old.

blanks.explanation: Io takes sono: io sono Marco.
Age takes avere: ho ventotto anni.

activities.hint: Name with essere, age with avere.

activities.en: My brother is ten years old.
activities.explanation: Mio fratello is one other person, so avere becomes ha: ha dieci anni.
activities.hint: Who comes first, then the verb, then the age.

activities.en: I am from Rome and I am ____.

blanks.explanation: A nationality is an adjective and agrees with you: italiano for a man, italiana for a woman. Inglese and francese have one form for both.

activities.hint: Type any nationality you like; it must agree with you.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Ciao! Io sono Giulia. E tu, di dove sei?
turns.en: Hi! I'm Giulia. And you, where are you from?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Ciao Giulia, piacere! Io ____ di Milano.
turns.en: Hi Giulia, nice to meet you! I am from Milan.

blanks.explanation: Io takes sono: io sono di Milano.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And how old are you?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: I am ____ and I am twenty-eight years old.

blanks.explanation: A nationality is an adjective: it agrees with you (italiano / italiana).
Age takes avere: ho ventotto anni.

reactions.it: Anche io sono italiana, di Napoli!
Che bello! Io sono di Napoli.
Che bello! Io sono di Napoli.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And what do you do for work?

blanks.explanation: After sono a job has no article: sono studente, sono insegnante.

reactions.en: Me too! I study in Bologna.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Bene! Ci vediamo dopo alla festa.
turns.en: Good! See you later at the party.

activities.template: Mia madre ____ insegnante e ____ quaranta anni.
activities.en: My mother is a teacher and she is forty years old.

blanks.explanation: Mia madre is one other person: è.
Age takes avere, and for one other person that is ha.

activities.hint: Lui / lei forms: è and ha.
Essere says who someone is, avere says what they have.
examples: Mia sorella ha un'amica a Milano.

lessons.title: Cosa faccio
lessons.outcome: Say what you do every day with regular -are, -ere and -ire verbs.

activities.body: A regular verb changes its ending for each person. -are: mangio, mangi, mangia, mangiamo, mangiate, mangiano. -ere: leggo, leggi, legge, leggiamo, leggete, leggono. -ire: dormo, dormi, dorme, dormiamo, dormite, dormono.
activities.tip: The subject pronoun is often left out: mangio il pane already says who is eating.

activities.en: I eat pasta in the evening.
activities.answer: Io mangio la pasta la sera.
accepted: La sera io mangio la pasta.
activities.explanation: Who, verb, what, then when: io mangio la pasta la sera.
activities.hint: The time phrase goes at the end.

activities.template: La mattina io ____ un caffè e ____ il giornale.
activities.en: In the morning I drink a coffee and read the newspaper.

blanks.explanation: Io takes the -o ending: bevo.
Still io, so leggere becomes leggo.

activities.hint: Both verbs are about io.

activities.en: Marco ____ pizza.

blanks.explanation: Marco is lui, so an -are verb ends in -a (mangia, compra) and an -ere or -ire verb in -e (prende, preferisce).

activities.hint: Type any verb that fits: it will be conjugated for Marco.

activities.en: My brother sleeps a lot on Sundays.
activities.answer: Mio fratello dorme molto la domenica.
accepted: La domenica mio fratello dorme molto.
activities.explanation: Mio fratello is lui: dormire becomes dorme.
activities.hint: Who, verb, how much, when.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: What do you do in the morning?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: La mattina ____ un caffè e poi lavoro.
turns.en: In the morning I ____ a coffee and then I work.

blanks.explanation: Io takes the -o ending: bevo or prendo un caffè.

reactions.it: Anche io bevo un caffè la mattina!
reactions.en: I drink a coffee in the morning too!

reactions.it: Un caffè al bar? Buona idea.
reactions.en: A coffee at the bar? Good idea.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: E la sera? Cucini a casa?
turns.en: And in the evening? Do you cook at home?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Sì, la sera ____ la pasta e ____ un libro.
turns.en: Yes, in the evening I cook pasta and read a book.

blanks.explanation: Io takes -o: cucino.
Io takes -o: leggo.

reactions.it: La pasta, che buona! Io invece ordino sempre una pizza.
reactions.en: Pasta, how nice! I always order a pizza instead.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And do you go to sleep early?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: No, I always go to sleep late.

blanks.explanation: Io takes -o: dormo.

reactions.en: Late! I go to sleep early instead.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Alright, good night then!

activities.template: Noi ____ il pane e i ragazzi ____ l'acqua.
activities.en: We buy the bread and the boys drink the water.

blanks.explanation: Noi takes -iamo: compriamo.
I ragazzi are loro: bevono.

activities.hint: Noi ends in -iamo, loro ends in -ono or -ano.
Pick who, a verb and what; add when or where if you like.
examples: Io mangio il pane la mattina.
I ragazzi bevono un caffè al bar.

lessons.title: Mi piace
lessons.outcome: Say what you like and do not like with mi piace and mi piacciono.

activities.prompt: Mi piace + one thing, mi piacciono + many
activities.body: Piacere works the other way round: the thing you like is the subject of the verb. One thing, or an action in the infinitive: mi piace. Several things: mi piacciono. Non goes in front.
activities.tip: Ti piace…? asks what someone else likes. Mi piace also goes with a verb in the infinitive: mi piace dormire.

activities.en: I like the sea.
activities.explanation: Il mare is one thing, so the verb is piace.
activities.hint: One thing: piace.

activities.template: Mi ____ la musica, ma non mi ____ i film.
activities.en: I like music, but I don't like films.

blanks.explanation: La musica is singular: piace.
I film is plural: piacciono.

activities.hint: Look at the thing that is liked: one or many?

activities.en: I really like ____.

blanks.explanation: After mi piace the thing takes its article: la pizza, il mare, la musica.

activities.hint: Type any singular thing you like; it gets its article.

activities.en: I like eating at the restaurant.
activities.explanation: After mi piace an action stays in the infinitive: mangiare, not mangio.
activities.hint: The action is not conjugated.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: What do you like to eat?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: I like ____.

blanks.explanation: One thing with its article: mi piace la pizza.

reactions.it: Anche a me! Andiamo in pizzeria stasera?
reactions.en: Me too! Shall we go to a pizzeria tonight?

reactions.it: Il gelato! Anche a me piace molto.
reactions.en: Ice cream! I like it a lot too.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And do you like sports?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Yes, I like football a lot.

blanks.explanation: Il calcio is one thing: mi piace.

reactions.it: Il calcio! Io preferisco il tennis.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Do you like cooking?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: No, non mi piace ____. Mi piace mangiare!
turns.en: No, I don't like cooking. I like eating!

blanks.explanation: After mi piace the verb stays in the infinitive: cucinare.

reactions.en: Then let's go to the restaurant!

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Perfect, pizza tonight!

activities.template: Mi ____ il mare e mi ____ le montagne.
activities.en: I like the sea and I like the mountains.

blanks.explanation: Il mare is singular: piace.
Le montagne is plural: piacciono.

activities.hint: Singular or plural?
Who likes or misses one thing? The verb agrees with the thing, which is singular here, so it stays piace or manca.
examples: A Marco manca il mare in estate.

lessons.title: Dove e quando
lessons.outcome: Add where and when to a sentence: a casa, al bar, in ufficio, la mattina, stasera, il lunedì.

activities.body: A place or time phrase goes at the end of the sentence, or at the start for emphasis. Places: a casa, al bar, in ufficio, in centro. Times: la mattina, la sera, stasera, oggi. Il lunedì, with the article, means every Monday.

examples.it: Io lavoro in ufficio la mattina.
examples.en: I work in the office in the morning.
I eat pizza at the restaurant.

examples.it: Stasera guardiamo un film a casa.
examples.en: Tonight we are watching a film at home.

examples.it: Il lunedì Anna studia in biblioteca.
examples.en: On Mondays Anna studies in the library.

activities.tip: A + il becomes al: al bar, al cinema, al mare. Casa and scuola keep a plain a: a casa, a scuola.

activities.en: In the evening I read at home.
activities.explanation: A casa takes a plain a. The time phrase can open or close the sentence.
activities.hint: Casa does not take an article here.

activities.template: La mattina lavoro ____ ufficio e la sera mangio ____ casa.
activities.en: In the morning I work in the office and in the evening I eat at home.

blanks.explanation: Ufficio takes in: in ufficio.
Casa takes a plain a: a casa.

activities.hint: In ufficio, a casa.

activities.en: I study Italian ____.

blanks.explanation: A time word or phrase closes the sentence: la sera, il lunedì, stasera, oggi, domani.

activities.hint: Type a time word like oggi or domani if you prefer.

activities.en: On Mondays my mother works at the bar.
activities.answer: Il lunedì mia madre lavora al bar.
accepted: Mia madre lavora al bar il lunedì.
activities.explanation: Mia madre is lei, so lavorare becomes lavora. Il lunedì means every Monday.
activities.hint: The day can open or close the sentence.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Hi! Where do you work?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: I work ____.

blanks.explanation: In ufficio, in centro; a casa, a scuola; al bar (a + il).

reactions.it: Anche io lavoro in ufficio, in centro.
reactions.en: I work in an office too, in the centre.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: And when are you at home?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: I am at home ____.

blanks.explanation: A time phrase at the end: la sera, il sabato, stasera.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Allora mangiamo insieme? Al ristorante o a casa tua?
turns.en: Then shall we eat together? At the restaurant or at your place?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Let's eat ____!

blanks.explanation: Al ristorante (a + il) or a casa mia.

reactions.it: Ottimo, conosco un posto in centro.
reactions.en: Great, I know a place in the centre.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Perfect, see you soon!

activities.hint: Who, verb, what, and then where or when.
examples: Io leggo il giornale al bar.
Gli amici guardano un film a casa.

lessons.title: Domande
lessons.outcome: Ask yes/no questions and dove, quando, chi and che cosa questions, and give short answers.

activities.body: A yes/no question keeps the words of the statement: only the voice goes up at the end. Dove (where), quando (when), chi (who) and che cosa (what) go at the start, right before the verb.
activities.tip: Short answers are normal: Sì. No. A Roma. Alle otto. Un panino. You do not need to repeat the whole sentence.

activities.en: Where does your mother work?
activities.explanation: Dove opens the question; tua madre is lei, so the verb is lavora.
activities.hint: The question word comes first.

activities.template: ____ abiti? A Roma. ____ parte il treno? Alle otto.
activities.en: ____ do you live? In Rome. ____ does the train leave? At eight.

blanks.explanation: The answer is a place, so the question is dove.
The answer is a time, so the question is quando.

activities.hint: Read the answer: a place or a time?

activities.template: ____ è quella ragazza? È mia sorella. ____ mangi stasera? Una pizza.
activities.en: ____ is that girl? She is my sister. ____ are you eating tonight? A pizza.

blanks.explanation: The answer is a person, so the question is chi.
The answer is a thing, so the question is che cosa.

activities.hint: A person or a thing?

activities.en: Are you going to the cinema tonight?
activities.explanation: A yes/no question has no question word: the statement order stays, only the voice rises.
activities.hint: No question word is needed.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Pronto? Ciao, sono Anna. Dove sei?
turns.en: Hello? Hi, it's Anna. Where are you?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Hi Anna! I am ____.

blanks.explanation: A place answers dove: a casa, al bar, in ufficio, alla stazione, in centro.

reactions.en: At the station! So you're leaving today.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Listen, what are you doing tonight?

turns.speaker: you
turns.template: Stasera ____ un film a casa. Vieni?
turns.en: Tonight I am ____ a film at home. Are you coming?

blanks.explanation: Io takes -o: guardo or vedo un film.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Yes! At what time?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: At nine. Is that okay?

blanks.explanation: Clock times take alle: alle nove.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Great, see you tonight!

activities.template: Lavori il sabato? ____, il sabato non lavoro.
activities.en: Do you work on Saturdays? ____, on Saturdays I don't work.

blanks.explanation: Non lavoro means the answer is no.

activities.hint: Read the second half of the answer.
Answer a question in full: who, verb, what, and where or when.
examples: Io aspetto il treno alla stazione.
Mio padre guarda un film stasera.

lessons.title: Come stai?
lessons.outcome: Hold your first full conversation: greet, say how you are, and make a plan.

activities.prompt: How are you? Essere + adjective, avere + noun
activities.body: Come stai? asks how you are. Answer with sto bene or così così, with essere + an adjective that agrees with you (sono stanco, sono stanca), or with avere + a noun: ho fame, ho sete, ho sonno.
activities.tip: Hunger, thirst and sleepiness are things you 'have' in Italian: ho fame, ho sete, ho sonno. Tiredness is something you 'are': sono stanco / stanca.

activities.en: Hi Marco, how are you?
activities.explanation: How are you uses stare, not essere: come stai?
activities.hint: Greeting, name, then the question.

activities.en: Fine thanks, but I'm tired.

blanks.explanation: Io takes sono: sono stanco.

activities.hint: Tired goes with essere.

activities.en: Marco is sleepy, but we are hungry.

blanks.explanation: Sonno goes with avere; Marco is lui: ha sonno.
Fame goes with avere; noi: abbiamo fame.

activities.hint: Sonno and fame take avere.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.en: Hi! How are you?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Fine thanks, but ____.

blanks.explanation: Sono + an adjective that agrees with you (stanco / stanca), or ho + fame, sete, sonno.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Senti, stasera c'è un film al cinema. Vieni?
turns.en: Listen, there's a film at the cinema tonight. Are you coming?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Yes, I'd love to! Let's go together.

blanks.explanation: Andiamo, the noi form, also means let's go.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Il film è alle nove. Prima mangiamo qualcosa?
turns.en: The film is at nine. Shall we eat something first?

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: Yes, I'm hungry! A pizza?

blanks.explanation: Fame goes with avere: ho fame.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.it: Allora pizza alle sette e film alle nove. A stasera!
turns.en: Pizza at seven and the film at nine, then. See you tonight!

turns.speaker: you
turns.en: See you tonight, ____!

blanks.explanation: Ciao, a dopo or a presto all close a friendly chat; buonanotte is for when the day is over, not before meeting tonight.

activities.en: I'm sleepy, I'm going home.
activities.explanation: Sonno goes with avere: ho sonno. Then vado a casa.
activities.hint: Sleepiness is something you have.

activities.en: Today I am ____ because it's Saturday.

blanks.explanation: The adjective agrees with you: contento or libero for a man, contenta or libera for a woman. Felice is the same for both.

activities.hint: Type any adjective that describes how you feel.
Make a plan: who, wants or has what, and where or when.
